title: Hydration
description: Learn about Angular hydration: how it works, how to enable it with provideClientHydration, event replay, DOM mismatch constraints, skipping hydration with ngSkipHydration, and debugging application stability.

blocks.text: Hydration is the process that restores the server-side rendered application on the client. This includes things like reusing the server rendered DOM structures, persisting the application state, transferring application data that was retrieved already by the server, and other processes.
Why is hydration important?

Hydration improves application performance by avoiding extra work to re-create DOM nodes. Instead, Angular tries to match existing DOM elements to the application's structure at runtime and reuses DOM nodes when possible. This results in a performance improvement that can be measured using Core Web Vitals (CWV) statistics, such as reducing the First Input Delay (FID / INP) and Largest Contentful Paint (LCP), as well as Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS). Improving these numbers also affects things like SEO performance.

Without hydration enabled, server-side rendered Angular applications will destroy and re-render the application's DOM, which may result in a visible UI flicker. This re-rendering can negatively impact Core Web Vitals like LCP and cause a layout shift. Enabling hydration allows the existing DOM to be re-used and prevents a flicker.
How do you enable hydration in Angular
Hydration can be enabled for server-side rendered (SSR) applications only.
Using Angular CLI

If you've used Angular CLI to enable SSR (either by enabling it during application creation with ng new --ssr or later via ng add @angular/ssr), the code that enables hydration should already be included in your application.
Manual setup
If you have a custom setup, you can enable hydration manually by importing provideClientHydration from @angular/platform-browser and adding that provider to your app's bootstrapping providers list:
Make sure that the provideClientHydration() call is also included into a set of providers that is used to bootstrap an application on the server (in app.config.server.ts).
Verify that hydration is enabled
After you've configured hydration and have started up your server, load your application in the browser:

items: Console DevTools: While running an application in dev mode, you can confirm hydration is enabled by opening Developer Tools. You should see a message that includes hydration-related stats, such as the number of components and nodes hydrated.

Angular DevTools: You can also use the Angular DevTools browser extension to see hydration status of components on a page, including an overlay indicating hydrated parts and highlighting hydration mismatch errors.

blocks.text: Capturing and replaying events

When an application is rendered on the server, it is visible in a browser as soon as produced HTML loads. Users may assume they can interact with the page, but event listeners are not attached until hydration completes. The Event Replay feature captures all events that happen before hydration and replays them once hydration has completed.
Event replay is enabled alongside incremental hydration. If you opt out of incremental hydration with withNoIncrementalHydration(), you can still enable event replay using withEventReplay():

code: import { bootstrapApplication, provideClientHydration, withEventReplay, withNoIncrementalHydration } from '@angular/platform-browser';

blocks.text: Constraints

Hydration imposes a few constraints on your application. Your application must have the same generated DOM structure on both the server and the client. This also includes whitespaces and comment nodes that Angular produces during rendering on the server.
Direct DOM Manipulation

If you have components that manipulate the DOM using native DOM APIs (such as document.getElementById(), appendChild, innerHTML, or outerHTML), the hydration process will encounter errors because Angular cannot resolve these untracked changes.
Valid HTML structure
Common cases of invalid HTML structure that result in DOM mismatch errors include:

items: <table> without a <tbody> (modern browsers automatically insert a <tbody> element, causing a mismatch).

blocks.text: Preserve Whitespaces Configuration
We recommend using the default setting of false for preserveWhitespaces. If you choose to enable it, ensure it is set consistently in tsconfig.server.json and tsconfig.app.json.

Hydration Timing and Application Stability

Hydration and post-hydration processes occur once the application has reported stability. Delays can be caused by intervals, timeouts, unresolved promises, or pending microtasks. The provideStabilityDebugging utility helps identify why your application fails to stabilize by logging pending tasks to the console.
I18N

Incremental Hydration
Incremental hydration is an advanced form of hydration that allows for more granular control over when hydration happens. See the Incremental Hydration guide for more details.
